.qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r9/rules/projects/webdev-task-template/instruction.md, environment/instructions/notes.md, environment/instructions/integration.md (template placeholders / shared runtime note)
evidence: instruction.md reads as a first-person request from a recruiting lead, not generated prose. Line 1 opens with a direct ask and a short sentence ('Can you build HireOps, the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day? Two things happen in it.'), followed by a plain statement of the hard part ('so the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled when someone else acts'). Line 3 is written from the user's side ('The order of cards inside a stage is ours to arrange', 'tell me why ... tell me who', 'I often move several candidates together'). Line 7 says 'never touch my draft or my cursor', and line 11 says 'layout and names are yours ... We don't need theme switching or a special phone layout.' Contractions appear throughout (counted with grep: don't x2, it's, mustn't, nobody's, people's). Sentence length varies from short ('Two things happen in it.', 'Candidates sign in too.') to longer compound sentences, so the cadence is not uniform. The file has no bullet lists or numbered acceptance items. A case-insensitive grep over instruction.md and both notes for seamless|robust|delve|leverage|intuitive|elevate|comprehensive|ensure|utiliz|cutting|streamline|empower and the em dash returned nothing. The runtime paragraph (line 13) is denser, but it keeps the speaker's voice ('How you lay the other files and routes out under /app is your call', 'so don't install packages', 'The browser side is free to pull fonts or a script from a CDN if that helps'). In the voice-consistency test between the instruction and the notes, hireops_rules.md is a team working document and sits in a more formal register with headings, tables and some bullets. It is still clearly the same 'we/our' team ('These are the working rules for HireOps, our recruiting workspace', 'what we care about is that the workspace behaves the way this note says', 'Each application has one conversation between our side and the candidate', 'Where drafts are kept is yours'). Its bullets are uneven in length and structure, not mechanically parallel. That register shift is normal between a chat request and a reference note and is not a voice break. Its §8 'Runtime file paths' (lines 196-202) and integration.md are impersonal runtime boilerplate shared with the template (template integration.md lines 1-14 are identical; the task adds a symlink paragraph). Under quality-checks.md this is acceptable infrastructure text and not LLM gloss. Two cosmetic observations, neither a voice defect: hireops_rules.md lines 99, 112, 173 and 180 break the file's ~105-column hard wrap (they look like spliced edits; the wording is unaffected), and the instruction mixes 'honour' (line 13) with the notes' 'honoring' / 'Honor' (integration.md line 8, hireops_rules.md line 201). That spelling mix belongs to check 3 if anywhere and reads as human inconsistency, not machine polish. Broken-app and conforming-alternative probes do not apply: this row grades only the prose of the brief, and no app behavior or judge output bears on it. No runtime evidence is needed for this row, so nothing missing is being waived.
